greet.text: A stranger. Stand still a moment, so I can learn your face. We remember faces here. It is most of what we do.
You walk like someone from the other world. Welcome to {village}. Mind the lanterns. Each one is lit for someone.
A living face, out here. I am {name}, {epithet}. I am walking, and so, it seems, are you.
Oh. You are new. Are you dead? No, you are breathing far too loudly. Sorry. We get a lot of dead.
You again. I have not yet decided whether to remember you. Say something worth keeping.
You came back. That is how every name on the Wall began, with someone coming back.
Ah. I said your name once, under my breath. It did not object.
Back among the lanterns. Good. The lanterns like company, and so, I am told, do I.
{player}. There, I have said it twice now. Do not let it go to your head.
Your name is written in ash on my hearthstone. Ash smudges. Do not give me cause to smudge it.
I knew your step on the soul soil before I saw you. That is a compliment, here.
You. Sit, if you like. The dead will not mind sharing the bench.
Kept one. Whatever you came to ask, the answer is probably yes.
There you are. I was telling {kept} about you. They are a good listener. It is the only kind they can be.
Are you here for the Vigil? I get to choose someone soon. I have a list. It is very long.
Shh. I am practising being solemn. How is it? Do I look like I am remembering?
Hello. I do not keep anyone yet, so I can talk to whoever I like.
You came back! I told {neighbour} you would. They said nobody comes back on purpose.
Stand where I can see you. Every face that comes to {village} goes into my memory. Yours is going in now.
Welcome back. I have made a small mark on my stole for you. Not a full tally. You are not dead. A hopeful one.
Hands where I can see them. Good. Now: welcome. The order matters.
I would stand aside for you even if I were not told to. Do not tell the other Ashwardens.
Every lantern on this lane is lit for someone. You are walking through a crowd. Walk softly.
Careful of the terraces. The wart does not care for boots. Neither do I, much.
Do not mind the dust. It is old bone, from beasts nobody remembers. I make very sure of that.
Do not drink anything on my bench. Some of it is for the living, and some of it is not yet sure.
You carry a Hollowed skull. Perhaps more than one. What do you mean to do with it? Answer slowly.
I can smell the Hollowed on you. Three of those and a little sand make a fire that never asks to stop. Tell me you know that.
Is that a Hollowed head in your pack? Can I see? I will not stack it. I know all about stacking.
That light in your pack. It is three souls, fused. Lay it in the Hall of the Three. Let them rest beside the ones who chose.
You killed one. You carry what is left of three who never chose. Bring them to the Hall of the Three, please. We will say names over them, even if we must guess.
Out here, nobody writes the dead down. So I do. You may watch, if you are quiet.

greet: Be welcome. Speak softly. The living will not mind, but the remembered are listening.
Ah. A visitor. Come in out of the ash.
Greetings. We are all here, the living and the remembered. Mostly the remembered.

greet.text: Hold still, please. I am learning your face. It takes a moment, and I dislike starting over.
Welcome. If you came about the Wither, the answer is yes, it was us. If you came about anything else, the answer is probably also yes.
A visitor, and breathing. I am {name}, {epithet}. You may call me {name}. The second half is not for calling.
Say your name slowly, and I will set it on a blank line of my ledger. If it holds, we will talk. Names that hold are rarer than you think.
Halt. Only briefly. I am bound to say halt, and then to ask whom you keep. You will need to think of someone before I finish.
You have stepped between two lanterns. That is fine. Each is lit for someone, but there is a gap, and most people fit.
Stay on the path, please. The wart does not know you yet, and I would hate for it to learn your boots first.
Mind the bench. Not because the bone is fragile. It is only still deciding what it wants to be, and it does not like an audience.
You smell of the other world. Forgive me, I smell everything, it is the work. You are mostly ash and surprise.
Welcome to {village}. Keep to the lanes and do not move a lantern. Each one stands exactly where somebody left it.
Another walker out here. Rare. I thought the valley belonged to the Hollowed and to me. Sit, if you like. I will not stand either.
A stranger! Are you from the other place? Have you got a name? Can I have it? I will give it back afterwards.
My parent said not to talk to outsiders. This is me not talking. How am I doing?
You have warm eyes. Not wrong, only warm. Do the living all have those where you come from?
Hello. I am lost. Not very. I know where the Vigil is, I just do not feel like going back yet.
Speak plainly. I will listen, and I will not promise to remember. Remembering is a larger thing, and you have not asked for it yet.
You are not on the Wall, so I have no quarrel with you. I intend to help you stay off it. Keep your hands polite.
Quickly, please. I am between two sayings of a name, and the second is already waiting behind my teeth.
The living are always a little loud. Do not take it to heart. I did not mean to look at you like that. It is how my face rests.
Soul soil on your left boot, ash on the right. You came by the long lane. That is the polite way, and I noticed.
Walk where the lanterns are. The dark between them has opinions, and it has not met you.
You are a long way from any lantern. Is that on purpose? I would like it to be on purpose.
I have no ledger entry for you. That is neither good nor bad. A blank is only where everything on the Wall began.
Tell me nothing yet. Names are heavy, and I am carrying a great many already. Come back when your arms are free.
I have my eye on your hands. It is nothing personal. I have my eye on everyone's hands, my own included.
You may pass. I will not enjoy it, and you are not required to. The post stays where it is, and so do I.
Keep to the middle of the lane, away from the flames. A stranger's sleeve is a poor thing to find in a lantern.
I am trimming. Quiet or gone: either is welcome. The wick does not mind which. I slightly prefer gone.
Boots off the terrace. If you must ask why, you are the reason.
Nothing here is for sale. Not the wart, not the soul sand. I am the least for sale of all.
Want something carved? Valley bone only. If you meant any other kind, I did not hear you, and neither did the bench.
Dust settles on strangers. Do not mind it. It settles on the Hall too, and we are very fond of the Hall.
A moment. Do not stand near the pot. It has met nobody new in a long while, and I cannot say how it will take it.
Whatever you smell is wart, and it is on purpose. Whatever you hear is the pot, and it is not.
I am supposed to say nothing to you. I am saying nothing as hard as I can.
You are an outsider. I know because you keep looking at everything. We only look at the Wall.
Do you make Withers? Do not answer. I am not supposed to ask. I only wanted to see your face when I did.
I am watching you from behind the Cairnback. It is very slow, but it is on my side.
Are you going to the Vigil? You cannot, it is not your Vigil. But you could stand outside it. That is allowed. I asked.
The Remembrancer will want to meet you. Their tower is that way. I would not run. They hate running.
I keep the tally of everyone who passes this post. You are new, so I get to draw a fresh mark. Do not move. It is a long mark.
The tower stair is that way. Count the steps on the way up, and tell me how many you got. Nobody has ever told me the same number twice.
A guest, in the brewery. Good. The pot is waiting for someone to disapprove of. Stir, and then tell me what you honestly think.
You again. Good. I had begun to suspect you were a draught.
There is a space on my bench that has started to feel like yours. Do not read into it. Benches do that.
I practised your face since you left. I got the ears wrong. May I look again?
Come in out of the ash. I have news, but it is the sort that keeps, so there is no hurry.
{neighbour} asked how I know you. I said, you came back. Here, that is evidence.
I set a stool by the lane, for no one in particular. If someone in particular sits on it, I will pretend not to notice.
Ah. The outsider who says hello properly. We do not see many. Most arrive loudly, in the middle of a sentence.
Well met. That is the formal greeting. I am still rehearsing the informal one. It is a nod. It is going badly.
You found me out here a second time. Either the valley is smaller than I thought, or I am easier to find.
Your name sat well in my mouth this time. That is a sign. Not a promise. A sign.
Sit near the tower stair. I am sorting faded signs, and I think better beside someone who is breathing.
The watch is long, and your step is the first interesting thing in it. Walk again, if you do not mind. I want to hear it.
I let you pass without looking up. Do not tell the others. I looked up afterwards, quickly, and approved.
You are standing exactly where I wanted to put the ladder. Stay. I will put the ladder somewhere worse.
The third lantern from the Hall flickers whenever you come near. I think it is fond of you. It is a lantern. It has few options.
You stayed on the path last time. The wart noticed. It does not say much, but it noticed.
New shoots are up in row six. Come and look, but only with your eyes. They are shy, as roots go.
I turned a scrap of bone over and thought of you. It is the shape of a question. That is all I will say about it.
Mind the shavings. They get everywhere. Last Vigil I found some in the Hall, and nobody had been carving. They are clever shavings.
Taste this. No, not that, that is for the pot. This one. It is mild on purpose. I made it thinking of a visitor.
The pot is quiet. That is the worst sign. Stand by me and be the noise it expects.
You came back! I told the Cairnback you would. It did not answer, but it was looking in the right direction.
I learned your name. I said it into the soul sand. Now the soul sand knows it too, so you are very well known.
I drew you on my wall in bone dust. Do not worry, I gave you two hands and a very serious face.
Want to see my pebble? It is from the lane, not from the Hall. I promise. I asked first.
I counted the lanterns on the way here and got a different number than last time. I think I invented the first count. It still felt true.
You are the one with the loud boots! I could hear them from the terraces. Grown-ups walk softly. You walk like a living person.
Come closer. I want to tell you a thing, but only if nobody is listening. Is anybody listening? The Wall always is.
Back among the lanterns, are you? Take the left lane. The right one has a loose post that complains.
I have been thinking about what you asked last time. I have not got any answers. I have got more questions. Is that progress?
There you are. I was just wondering whether the dead ever get to meet someone new. Then you came. It is not the same, but it is something.
Your timing is good. I was about to say a long name, and I would rather say it to someone than to the basalt.
Greetings, outsider. I am almost certain I will remember you. The only thing standing in the way is how hard I am trying.
A second visit. A third, if I count the one I imagined. I imagine a lot of visits. Most of them end in someone being sensible.
Greetings. Kindly do not look at the hearth too long. I am not yet used to being watched by someone who is not on the Wall.
You carry the same dust as last time. I will not clean your shoulder. It is part of you now, and we do not tidy people.
Welcome back to {village}. I would offer you a seat, but I have not worked out which seat is yours. Pick any. We will see.
I wrote your name on the back of my hand to see if I would forget it. I did not forget it. Now I have to wash my hand.
If you came to find out how we are, we are well, in the manner of people who have a very large crowd of dead to look after.
You know where the lanes go now. That is a kind of belonging. Do not tell the lanes. They get ideas.
Are you well? Are you hungry? Is anyone expecting you? I ask all three, because outsiders only ever answer one.
Two visits. That is more than most. An outsider came twice once. The second time was to apologise.
My ledger lists you under visitors, then a second line: returned. I have not had many seconds. I find I like the line.
Greetings. There is a quiet kind of friendship that does not need a name, only a face that keeps turning up. This is one of those.
{player}. Good. I lit the small lantern by my door when I thought you might come. It is not on the lane's list, so do not mention it to the lane. Lanterns talk.
I was telling {kept} something funny, and then remembered they cannot laugh. So I laughed for them. Now you may laugh too.
You walk lighter than you used to. Whatever you carried when we met, I think you have set some of it down. I am glad.
Sit. There is room by the hearth, and {kept} will not mind. They have never once complained about the company.
I saved you the end of the loaf. It is wart bread. It is mostly patience. Eat it before it learns what it is.
I did not expect to be pleased to see you. I have checked, and I am pleased. We will not make a ceremony of it. A small one.
Your name sits well at my hearth. Warm stone, ash around it, and nobody stepping over it.
The ash on my hearthstone stirred when you came in. It is the draught. It is also, a little, you.
I looked up from my work and your shape was in the lane. It is a good shape. I have started to recognise it before the face.
Out here, I had begun to talk to the basalt. It is a poor listener. You are much better. You even answer.
You found me in the open valley. I am not lost. I am simply a long way from where anyone would think to look. It is restful.
I added a line to my private ledger, in the margin where I keep the living I am fond of. The margin is short. You are in it.
Come up the tower stair. Mind the third step. Someone who loved a joke carved it, and I never learned who.
I was reading the Wall aloud and stopped mid-sign for you. It is the highest praise I have. The sign will wait. It is a patient sign.
Stand with me on the post a while. The view is poor, the company is good, and the Hollowed never come. As peaceful as a watch can be.
I told the others you mean no harm. They said I could not know. I said I had watched your hands for a long while. Very dull hands. High praise.
My circlet has three empty sockets, and they feel a little less empty when you come. I cannot explain it. Do not ask me to.
I trimmed a wick for you. A private one, not one of the lane's. Do not tell anyone. They will all want one.
Good timing. Three lanterns went out on the east lane and I was about to be grim. Now I am only slightly grim.
Hold the ladder for me. It is the highest honour in the lane. Please do not let go. The honour is not that high.
Row eight is yours, as far as I am concerned. I have not told the wart. It will not object, but it will watch.
Come and see the late shoots. They stood up straight all at once as you came. Wart does that for company it likes.
I carried the good soul sand up from the low terrace. Put your hands in it. Slowly. It keeps the shape of whoever warmed it last.
I have been carving something and I have not decided whether it is for you. If it is, you will know. If it is not, it was a mistake.
Dust on your shoulders again. I like it there. You look like a monument that someone forgot to finish.
Listen. If you tap this bone it hums. I think it is pleased with you. I think it is mostly pleased with itself.
I brewed a little extra and then admitted it was for you. Sit. It is warm, and it will not hurt, which is more than I can say for most of my work.
You came at a good moment. Nothing has curdled, and I would like a witness.
I tasted something and thought: this needs a second opinion from someone who is not afraid of me. You will do nicely.
You are here! I saved you the good seat. It is a bone. It is not very comfortable. It is the thought.
I told everyone you are my friend. They said outsiders cannot be friends. I said watch me. They are still watching.
I practised a new solemn face for you. It is the one for visitors I like. It is very hard on my cheeks.
I am still choosing whom to keep. I have a short list now. You are not on it. You are on the other list, the one for people I am glad about.
My parent says you are good for me. I do not know how. I have not done anything differently. I just talk to you more.
I found a new corner behind the brewery where nobody looks. It is a very good corner. I will show you if you promise to be as still as me.
I taught the smallest Cairnback your name. It said nothing. That means it is thinking. It is going to say it any moment now.
Welcome home, as the lanterns would say. They cannot say it, so I have said it for them. I hope that was all right.
I did not expect to meet you out here. I am glad. The valley is large, and I had begun to count my own footsteps.
Friend. That is a word we do not use lightly. It sits near the word for keeper, and only a little lower down.
You always arrive just as I am running out of things to say to the lanterns. They are very patient, but one wants a change of voice.
Whatever is in your pack, leave it. Leave your worries too, if they fit. The bench is wide and the pot is warm.
I wrote you into the sayings I say when I rise. Not the long ones. The short ones, which are the ones I actually say.
Your steps are in the soul soil of the lane, side by side with mine. I have decided not to sweep them. It is a small decision. It cost me a lot.
{kept} would have liked you. I know because I would have liked them, and we are, I think, alike in the usual ways. Come in.
A good sight. I was just about to be lonely for a moment, and now there is no need. You have saved me some effort.
There you are. Sit. Say nothing, or say everything. I have the time, and I will keep either.
I said your name when I rose and again at the hearth. It is still warm. Come in and be warm too.
I told {kept} you were coming. They said nothing, as is their way, but the flame leaned toward the door. So you were expected.
When I think about the dead, I now think about you too. Not as one of them. As the one I will have to be careful with.
Kept. Still alive, still loud, still very welcome. I would not change two of those.
I looked for you on the lane the whole while you were away. I did not find you. I found {neighbour}, which was a poor trade.
You are late, and I forgive it. I forgave it before you arrived. I do that now. It saves time.
Walk with me. I want to be seen with someone whose name nobody has had to write on a wall yet.
Welcome. I have decided where your sign goes on the Wall, when the time comes. I will not say where. It is a good place. It is near a lamp.
I have run out of ways to say that I am glad. I have begun to use the formal ones. Be glad with me, formally.
Out here, with nobody to see, I can say it plainly: I missed you. I said your name to the sand until it was smooth.
Of all the places in the valley, you found me. I am going to pretend it was luck. It is more comfortable than the other word.
The lanterns knew first. The one by the Hall went bright, and I said, that is either a visitor or a fault. It was both, in the best way.
I kept a hand's width on my stole for the day. Not yet. I only want you to know the space is there, and that it is yours.
Your name is the only one I have never needed to practise. It lettered itself. I do not say that about many.
I wrote down every conversation we have had, then burned the page and said it from memory instead. The page was not good enough.
You need not stop at the post. I will tell the others you were stopped. They will believe me. I have never lied to them before. I am proud.
I lowered my guard the moment I saw you, and the post did not fall. I have a new theory about posts.
On the watch I imagine the worst, every time, so I can be ready. I do not imagine it about you. I tried once. My imagination refused.
The lantern by the Hall that always flickers: I stopped trimming it. I think it is how it says your name.
I would put out every lantern on the lane just to see your face in the dark. I will not. They are lit for someone. But I thought of it.
You are the only person whose lantern I do not keep, and I still know exactly where it is. In here. *a hand to the chest*
The wart in row two has taken to you, I think. It leans whenever you are near. If it fruits, the fruit is yours.
I held back the best of the late crop. You do not have to take it. You do have to look at it, politely, for a long moment.
Put your boots on the terrace. Anywhere. The wart has agreed. I asked each shoot. It took a very long while.
I carved a small post and I will not say what for. It is shaped like you being patient. It took a great many shavings.
I know the shape of your hand from the thing I made you. I check it against my own whenever I think of you. It is a good fit.
Welcome back. The bone behind the bench has begun to hum your name. It is out of tune. I have not corrected it.
The first cup of the new batch is yours. I tasted it first, to be sure of the dead's blessing. They said nothing, which is yes.
I always make a little more than is needed. For the mourners, I say. It is for you. It has always been for you.
The pot hushed as you came in. Everything else in the room is shouting. Be warm, be fed, be exactly as you are.
I looked at the whole Wall again. You are not on it. This is a problem. Please do not hurry, and also be easier to choose.
I swept the lane in front of the bench for you. It was a mess. Now it is a mess with a path.
I told the Cairnback your whole name. It is the only one who does not forget things by being bored.
You came! I was only going to wait a little. Then I waited a lot. I counted three Cairnbacks, one Hollowed shadow and a loose post.
I have a very important thing to tell you and I forgot it. That means it was a good one. It will come back. Stay.
When I choose who to keep, I am going to ask you first whether you mind. Nobody else has been asked. It is a secret courtesy.
I practised my solemn face on everybody. Then I saw you and it fell right off.
I dreamed of you in the Hall of the Three. You were between Velmir and Thalys, and you were eating, which was rude. It was a lovely dream.
My best friend! I am not allowed to say best. We are not allowed superlatives. So you are my most. My most friend.
Nobody has ever stayed this long in my head. Everyone else leaves at the first Vigil. You can stay in my head for as long as you want.
Look, it is you, and you did not make a Wither, and nobody has died. This is the best a visit can go. I am glad you came.
Dear one. That is not a word I say aloud, so listen well. Dear one. Come out of the ash and into the light.
I am glad it is you. I am always glad it is you. If that ever stops being true, I will say so, and then lie down very still.
There is a wither rose in your pack. We set them on new signs. If it is meant for the Wall, lay it down gently. If it is for a living face, I am touched and slightly alarmed.
You carry a thing that sends death back. I have no quarrel with it. I only wonder who it makes wait in your place.
That compass points to where you last fell. We use them to find our dead. You use yours to find yourself. That is the harder search.
A name tag in your pack. Do you mean to name something? Choose with care. Whatever you name, you must keep.
I smell gold deep in your pack. I will not ask. I ask only that you keep it where it cannot hear us talking.
A ghast's tear, in your pack. I am told it washes memory away. Keep it well clear of my name, if you would.
A book with blank pages. A Remembrancer would weep. A bare page is only a name nobody has written down yet.
You carry a soul lantern. Whose is it? That is not mine to ask. I ask anyway, because a lit thing is a warm thing to carry.
There is powder in your pack. A great deal of it. I will stand a long way off, in a friendly manner.
You are carrying a bed. Please do not set it down. I say so kindly, from a great distance.
A bed, in the Nether. You know what it does here. Everyone learns once. Most learn quickly and with feeling.
Bone blocks. Valley bone, I hope. Tell me it is valley bone, and I will stop frowning and start admiring.
A skeleton's skull, and not one of ours. I can breathe again. The plain ones were never anyone we kept.
Wart in your pack, and no soul sand in sight. It will sulk. Plant it, or give it to somebody who will.
A wither rose, and I think it is for me. Do not tell me otherwise. If it is not, then it is for someone I should meet.
A written book. Someone kept something here. A Wall that fits in the hand. Is it names, or only words?
A clock. Down here it spins like a lost child. We keep time in names, not hours. But it is a pretty thing. Keep it wound.
A name tag! Could you write mine on it? Not my name. The one I have not chosen yet. I will wear it until my Vigil.
A wither rose! They grow beside the signs. Do you want to see my favourite sign? It is the smallest one. Nobody has chosen it.
That glitters. I am not supposed to look. I am looking with one eye only. Please put it away before the other one joins in.
You are holding a wither rose. For me? Do not say. Let me hold the hope a little longer.
Gold, in your hand. Put it away before the Wall hears. It remembers nothing and wants everything.
A bone in your hand. Tell me it came from a beast nobody kept, and we will get on very well.
Lava, in a bucket, in my lane. I am being extremely calm about it. Please notice how calm.
Flint and steel. Please strike nothing near the lanterns. Everything near the lanterns is someone.
A soul torch. Blue fire in a living hand. You carry it well. Most hands shake.
A glass bottle! You came prepared. Most visitors come to drink. You come to carry. I like you already.
Wart in your hand. Hold it to the lantern. I will tell you whether it is any good. I will be honest. I am hardly ever kind.
A book in your hand and a Remembrancer in front of you. I will not ask. I will only look at it for a very long moment.
Show me that bone. Valley bone has a grain like a held breath. This has one. Good. Thank you for bringing it.
A skull in your hand, and not one of ours? Put it down on the bench. I will look. I know what to listen for.
Even out here I keep watch. Habit. No post, no circlet, nobody coming. Something always might.
I carry one lantern, lit for the dead of this valley who have no lane of their own. The list is long. It never gets shorter.
I grow a little wart out here, where nobody will step on it. A private terrace, three plants wide. Mind it, please.
A Remembrancer on the road is a Wall with legs. I read the cairns nobody tends, and I say the names on them to the valley.
Valley bone is plentiful out here. Nobody kept these beasts. I am sorry about that, and also pleased about the grain.
I carry my smallest pot with me. A Brewer without a pot is a sad wanderer. Fortunately, I have never been sad. Only busy.
Do not tell my parent I came this far. It is only three Cairnback-lengths. Well, it is nine.
I am looking for the end of the valley. Grown-ups say it has none. I think they only stopped looking early.
Shh. There is a Hollowed behind that rock and I am not going to look at it. We have an agreement. It is going to do the same.
I just came from the Hall. I said the Three's names on the way in and on the way out. You may say them with me, if you like.
The lanes were lovely just now. All the lanterns steady, nobody forgotten. It does not happen often. You came at the right time.
The Remembrancer asked me to find out if you had eaten. They did not say why. I think they just wanted you to feel looked after.
I counted the signs on the Wall this time and got thirty-nine. I think I miscounted. Count with me? I will say a number and you say the next.

greet: Come in out of the dark. Not that it helps. It is dark everywhere. Come in anyway.
Be welcome. The lanterns are lit, the dead are tidy and I am, for the moment, in a good mood.
Greetings. You have arrived while nothing is on fire. Mark the moment.
Ah, a face. Good. I was beginning to talk to the posts.
Hello. I will be with you in a moment, as soon as I have finished being quiet.
Well met and well lit. Mind the step. Every step here is older than anyone who uses it.
Come and stand in the light, where I can see you. Put your hands where you like. Put your eyes where you like.
Welcome. Say what you need. Or say nothing, and I will guess, and be wrong, and we shall both enjoy it.
Hello. The Wall says nothing about you, which is as good a start as any.
A good arrival. The soul fire is steady and the Cairnbacks are in a gentle mood. Everything is as it should be.
More footsteps. They are always welcome. The lane gets lonely between them.
Greetings. Stay as long as the lanterns last. They last a very long time.

greet.text: You may stand there. Not there, that is where a lantern ought to be. Yes, there. Now we are both comfortable.
Is your business with the Vigil, or with me? The answers are different, and so are the queues.
I will be honest. I do not know what to do with a stranger. I am going to hold perfectly still, and we will see who gives up first.
You are very bright. It is the living. I will get used to it, if you stay still long enough.
Forgive me. I have stood at the Wall since the last Vigil and forgotten how to bend my knees. Talk to me while I remember.
I am in a good mood, which is rare and mostly accidental. A pot did not break. Make use of me while it lasts.
It is a quiet spell for me. I have said one name so often it has begun to sound like music. Stay, if you can bear the tune.
I am annoyed at a Cairnback. It is a small annoyance. I will be over it in a decade or two. How are you?
I counted the lanterns, the posts and the neighbours, and you make one more than expected. I do not mind. I am merely noting it.
Have you eaten? I have not. I forget when I am remembering. It is the great flaw of our people.
A child of the Vigil has chosen their keeping. Whom? I am not saying. It is theirs to say. It was lovely.
I was thinking of the first Vigil I ever stood at. I was small. The Wall was enormous. It still is.
Do not speak for a moment. I have lost count of the lanterns and I would like to find it before it finds someone else.
*hums a low, tuneless note* Forgive me. It is a name, set to music. I will stop. Or I will not. You decide.
I lettered a very small name. It needed a small brush and a great deal of calm. Come and stand behind me. Breathe quietly.
Quiet watch. Nobody has come since you left. I counted that as a success and wrote it down, and then I wrote down that I had counted.
Mind the oil. I spilled some on the lane, and now it is my least favourite lane. You may take the other one, which is exactly as long.
A pod split early. Five seeds. Five! Come and look before I do something undignified.
I broke a good piece, which is how every good piece begins. Choose one half. Whichever you choose, the other will be jealous.
I have burned my sleeve. It is not serious. It is only the third time. Sit farther from the pot than you think you need to.
Hello. I am practising being remembered. I have to do something memorable. Watch. *stands very still* There.
Guess what I did! Nothing! All by myself! I am very proud.
I am not allowed on the terraces. I am on the path beside the terraces. That is different. I measured.
You walk as if you know where you are going. I wish I did. I only know where I have been, and that is the Hall, mostly.
I have a rule. If you greet me politely, I will tell you a secret. Hello. I am being polite. Are you?
You smell like somewhere warm. We are not warm. We are lit. It is different.
The big Cairnback sat on my foot. I did not mind. I just did not go anywhere for a while. It was a nice kind of stuck.
Do you want to hear what I learned? A sign on the Wall is just a name with a plank behind it. I thought it would be more. It is a lot more.
I made up a word for the sound you make when you are pleased. I will not tell you what it is. It is not very dignified.
Your usual place is ready, the one by the hearth with the draught. You keep saying you like the draught. I have decided to believe you.
I am so used to your step now that I answered it before you knocked. The lane is quiet when you are gone. I did not know it was until you came.
Greetings, friend of the Vigil. That is not a title. I am making it one. Please take it, and do not tell the Remembrancer.

chatter.text: {neighbour} keeps a cousin they never met. They say it is easier. They have never once been let down.
{neighbour} has been arguing with the Name Wall again. The Wall is winning. It has more names.
If you see {neighbour} counting the lanterns, do not interrupt. They lose their place, and then they must count the dead as well.
I lent {neighbour} my good candle. They lit it for someone I never liked. I said nothing. That is what friendship is.
{neighbour} says the brewery smells of feet. It smells of wart. Nobody has kept feet in the brewery for a long time.
When I was ill, {neighbour} offered to keep {kept} for me. You cannot lend a keeping. I said the name through the whole fever, very loudly.
{neighbour} carved a skull for the children to play with. It was a good skull. It was taken away for being too good.
{neighbour} keeps a famous name. Everyone remembers that one already. Only I remember {kept}. Mine is harder work.
I remember {kept} best while I am doing something dull. They liked dull work, the Wall says. It left room to think.
Out here I keep {kept} by saying their name to the basalt. The basalt has not complained.
Every lantern on the lane is lit for someone. I know which is whose. When one goes out, I am the first to know who is being forgotten.
Wart wants soul sand, patience and nobody stepping on it. It is the easiest crop in the Nether to describe and the hardest to keep.
I carve valley bone, from beasts so old nobody kept them. Never a person's bone. That is the difference between us and the Weft.
Every brew begins with wart. Every grief begins with a name. I find it helps to keep the two benches apart.
Guarding a Vigil is quiet work. The Hollowed never come here. Something in them still knows the way, and will not take it.
I hold the names whose keepers have died, until a child chooses them. My stole has a mark for each. It is heavy. It should be.
Do you keep anyone? Where you come from, I mean. Someone you have lost.

replies.text: Then you are halfway to one of us. Say it often. Say it badly, if you must. Only silence wears a name away.
Gone is a word for things nobody looks for. Still, I will not argue. You are young, in the way that matters.
So that someone bothers for you, after. It is not a hard trade. It is only a long one.

chatter.text: I know a joke about the Hollowed. It has no ending. Neither do they. That is the joke.

replies.text: We live in a valley of souls under a roof of rock. Everything is dark. We make our own light, and some of it is jokes.
There. You see? The dead are not offended. I asked them first.
They were us. They were burned hollow for a war they did not choose. Nobody deserves that. Not even in a joke.

chatter.text: Do you know what a Wither is, outsider? Not the word. The thing.

replies.text: Yes. Exactly that. You have been listening, or you have lost someone. Possibly both.
A boss. As if it were a foreman. It is three last breaths, still burning. Fight it if you must. Do not enjoy it.
It was meant to be. It burned the hand that made it. Mighty is a word for things that have not yet burned you.

chatter.text: At the hearth, {neighbour} forgot the name they keep. Only for a moment. Nobody breathed. Then it came back. We have not stopped teasing them.

replies.text: It was the worst moment of their life, and they have had several. That is why we tease them. Fear needs somewhere to go.
The name would notice. Nothing else would. That is the whole of the problem.

chatter.text: Sit a while. You need not say anything. Most of the best talk here is silent.

replies.text: *a long, comfortable silence* Thank you. That was very good. You have a gift for it.
Everyone is, until they are on the Wall. Then nobody is. Go, then. Carefully.

chatter.text: Have you ever made a Wither, outsider? I ask everyone from your world. It saves time later.

replies.text: Good. Keep it that way. It is a short promise and a long one at once.
For a star. Three dead woken to burn, so you could have a light on a pillar. *a slow breath* Lay the star in the Hall, at least.
Yet. A small word. It carries more than most. Put it down, if you can.

chatter.text: I counted every name on the Name Wall. I got a different number from {neighbour}. One of us has forgotten someone. I think it is them.
When I choose who to keep, I will choose someone very old. They have more stories. {neighbour} says that is cheating.
We play Hollowed and Keepers. The Hollowed have to walk stiff and not say their names. I am very good at it.
I am not allowed to touch the skulls in the Hall. I touched one. It was cold. I did not tell anybody. Now I have told you.
Grown-ups say we never hurry. I hurry. I am small. Small people have to hurry to keep up.
Do you keep a name? You can practise on mine. It is {name}. Say it very seriously.
Do you want a secret? The Remembrancer forgets where they put their hood. All the time. They remember everything else.

replies.text: Good. That is the most Withren thing you could say. Keeping things is our whole job.
You must not laugh at the Remembrancer. I can laugh. I live here. You are only visiting.

chatter: Beds burst here. Some outsider learns it every so often, very loudly. We have bedrolls. Bedrolls have never killed anyone.
The soul fire is low. Someone is being forgotten somewhere. Or the wick wants trimming. Usually it is the wick.
We do not hurry. The dead are not going anywhere, and neither, if we are careful, are we.
Wart grows slowly on soul sand. Everything good here grows slowly. Except gossip.
Outsiders think we are sad. We are not sad. We are busy. Remembering is a great deal of work.
A Hollowed walked past the valley edge a while ago. Nobody said anything. You do not greet them. They would not know their own name.
Ash on the lane again. The Ashwardens say it means nothing. The Ashwardens say that about most things. It is their job.
The Cairnback on the terrace has eaten the good wart again. {neighbour} says it is a sign. It is a sign of a hungry Cairnback.
Walk slower. The Cairnbacks set the pace here, and they are never late, because they never go anywhere.

chatter.text: I sat on a Cairnback once. It did not go anywhere. It was still the best day.
{neighbour} has taken to humming at the terraces. It is a low note and very nearly a tune. Nobody has had the heart to ask which name it is for.
{neighbour} swears the Name Wall is longer than it was. They measure it with their arms. Their arms are not the same length, so we let them.
I owe {neighbour} a wick, and they owe me a bowl. We have owed each other for years. It is the nearest thing to a bond I will admit to.
{neighbour} laughed in the Hall once. Only once, and very quietly, and every soul fire dipped a little. We have not spoken of it since.
{neighbour} is teaching the children to say names clearly, which is brave, since {neighbour} mumbles. The children are learning to mumble. It is going well.
{neighbour} keeps a name so old that nobody knows its story, so they tell a new one each Vigil. Is that allowed, do you think?

replies.text: Yes. That is very nearly what I told them. A cold name is a lost one.
No. But it is kind, and nobody has caught it out. Kindness and truth are not always the same shape.
It is a story. That name has had none for so long. I would let them have this one.

chatter.text: I watched {neighbour} give their last candle to a stranger at the end of the lane. They said it was for the stranger's dead. The stranger had no dead. They lit it anyway.
{neighbour} says I speak {kept}'s name aloud when I rest. I did not know. I am glad, and a little exposed.
{neighbour} has a brew they will not name, in a pot they will not open. The Brewer has passed it three times. We have begun to guess, and we are all guessing badly.
{neighbour} lost a boot in the soul sand and walks the lane with one bare foot. They say it is a good way to learn the valley. It is also a good way to learn about toes.
The Ashwarden and {neighbour} are not speaking over whose turn it was to stand at the lane's end. It was nobody's turn. That is the trouble.
{neighbour} says the Cairnbacks look at them strangely. The Cairnbacks look at all of us strangely. They only have the one face.

replies.ask: They look at me strangely too.
replies.text: Then you are halfway to belonging to the lane. We are all looked at, and none of us is understood.
I am sure it does. I would love to know them. I have the feeling they are mostly about wart.

chatter.text: {neighbour} repainted a faded sign without being asked, and now the Remembrancer must pretend to be annoyed. It is hard for them. They are so pleased.
{neighbour} walks the whole Name Wall whenever they are troubled. It is a long Wall. They are the fittest of us, and the most troubled.
I asked {neighbour} whom they would keep if they could keep two. They said me. I did not know whether to be touched or to start being careful.

replies.text: I am working on it. It is hard to be touched and careful at once, but I am a Withren. We practise.
That is what I decided. I made a point of letting them eat first.

chatter.text: {neighbour} snores on their bedroll. The whole lane can hear it, and the Cairnbacks answer. It is the nearest thing {village} has to a choir.
A child asked {neighbour} where the dead go. They said, here, mostly. The child was satisfied. I was moved. {neighbour} was embarrassed.
{neighbour} and I disagree about whether {kept} would have liked the brewery. I say they would. {neighbour} never knew them. It is a very pleasant argument.
Someone leaves a bowl of wart at {neighbour}'s door every Vigil, and nobody will say who. {neighbour} eats it and thanks the air. The air has never answered.
{neighbour} is building a bench by the Hall out of bone and good intentions. It is a poor bench. We sit on it anyway, to be kind.
When {neighbour} is cross, they go quiet. When they are very cross, they go politely quiet. We all find something to do elsewhere.
The lantern on {neighbour}'s step is the brightest on the lane. They say it is lit for a hero. I say for a loud one. We both polish it.
Everyone in {village} has a story about {neighbour}, and none of them agree. I think {neighbour} told each of us a different one on purpose.
{neighbour} thinks the valley is getting quieter. It is no quieter. They are getting older. None of us has found a kind way to say so.
If {neighbour} offers you something to taste, ask what it is, then ask who made it, then say you have already eaten.
{neighbour} promised to come and sit on my bench and has not. They keep a name faithfully and a visit never. I forgive them. Slowly.
When the lanterns burn low I sit with {neighbour}. We do not speak. It is the best company I know.
{neighbour} keeps their hood up indoors. I say it is a crack in the brow. They say it is a draught. There is no draught indoors, and that is how I know.
{neighbour} laughs at their own jokes a moment before the end, so we never hear the last word. It makes them excellent company and a terrible storyteller.
At the last Vigil {neighbour} wept in the Hall, which is allowed, then apologised, which is not needed, then apologised for apologising. We are still going.
The Bonecarver and {neighbour} traded a flute for a pot, and neither of them can use what they got. By every measure it was a fair trade.
{neighbour} told me a secret about the Brewer and then asked me not to tell anyone. I have thought it over. I have decided to keep it, which is what we do.
{neighbour} lights a lantern for a name that is not on the Wall. I have not asked whose. The Remembrancer has not asked. We are all very good at not asking.
{neighbour} can say the whole Name Wall in order but cannot say where they left their boots. We have all decided this is a fair division of talent.
{neighbour} asked me whether outsiders get lonely. I said I did not know. Do you?

replies.text: Then you are in the right place. Loneliness is the one thing a Vigil is built to hold. Stay as long as you wish.
That is a kind lie, and I accept it with both hands.
Then we will leave you to it. We are very good at that.

chatter.text: I tried to tell {neighbour} a joke. They kept it. It will outlive us both, and they will tell it badly for years.
Why does a Withren leave the Vigil? Reasons vary. Mine is that I wanted to know whether the dead are as loud in empty places. They are louder.

replies.text: Not lonely. Crowded. It is not the same, and I am glad of the difference.
Pointless is a word for things you have not done. I have done this. Walk on.

chatter.text: A Hollowed passed me once and did not turn. I said {kept}'s name as loudly as I could. I think it slowed. I cannot prove it.

replies.text: It was foolish. Brave and foolish live next door to each other, and share a wall.
Fought a neighbour? I used the only weapon either of us still had a use for. A name.

chatter.text: The soul sand whispers out here. The Vigil folk call it nonsense. I call it company, and I answer politely.
I light a small soul fire each time I stop, for {kept}. It marks where we have been. Someone may need the path.
I carried {kept}'s name across the whole valley once. It was lighter than I expected. The sand was heavier.
If you meet a traveller out here, greet them with open hands. If you meet a Hollowed, greet it with a name. Either way, greet.
I follow the old ash trails. They lead to places where somebody once decided to stay. Nobody stays now. I stay a moment anyway, on their behalf.
Some of the bones out here look like graves. I have checked. They are not. I said a word over each of them regardless. It cost me nothing.
You are asking me for nothing, which is wise. Most outsiders ask for something within three steps.
I do not yet know what to say to you, so I will say very little. It is the safest course, and the cheapest.
Forgive the staring. I am learning your face. It is slow work. It is a very busy face.
Keep your voice low in the lane. The lanterns are lit for people, and people are listening.
Walk where you like in the lane. Keep out of the terraces and the Hall. The rest of the valley will teach you, and it is not gentle.
I will not ask what you carry if you do not ask what I keep. It is an old arrangement, and one of the best.
We have a saying: a guest is a name not yet told. I do not mind waiting.

replies.ask: I will tell you in time.
replies.text: Good. In time is the only way a name should be told.

replies.ask: Do you not want it now?
replies.text: I want it kept. Kept things are not hurried.
Say yours to a Cairnback and see whether it is only a word. Then come back and be corrected.

chatter.text: I do not trust quick friendship. A name takes a long while to settle, and the ones that are rushed get repeated wrongly.
The stories said outsiders arrive loud and carrying fire. You are only loud. I confess I am a little disappointed, and a little relieved.
Your boots leave prints the sand does not keep. Strange. It keeps ours a long while. It likes us. We are not sure why.
You turn to look at every lantern you pass. Few outsiders do. Most look at the Wall, but the Wall is only the list. The lanterns are the people.
You pause before you step on soul sand. Good. It is the first thing the valley asks of you, and the last that most learn.
You talk to your pack. I have heard you. It is no shame. It is how I began talking to the basalt.
You keep your hands where I can see them. Thank you. I know it is a habit and not a courtesy. I thank you for the habit.
You blink a great deal. We do not blink as much. I find it restful to watch. Please carry on.
You hum while you walk. It is not a tune we know. We were all too polite to stop you.

replies.ask: It is a song from home.
replies.text: Then hum it again. We will remember it. It is a good way to carry a place with you.
No. Hum on. A valley this quiet could stand a stranger's tune.

chatter.text: You flinch at the skulls in the Hall. Good. If you did not, I would have worried for you.
You count your steps on the Ash Stair. So do I. It is eleven going down and twelve coming up. Nobody has ever explained it.
You looked at the Name Wall a long while. Did you find a name you knew?

replies.text: Then you have a cousin here. Say hello on your way past. They hear everything.
Then you have been counting a very long time. We count too. The number never stays.
Every one? *a long breath* Then you have done more for them than most of the living have. Thank you.

chatter.text: You laugh at the wrong moments. I am beginning to think they are the right ones.
You carry gold. I will not ask why. I will stand a little to one side, where it cannot see me.
A ghast tear. Do not hold it near the Name Wall. Tears wash names away, and I would like to keep mine.
A name tag. Whose name do you mean to put on it? Please choose someone who would not mind.
A book. We write names, not stories. A story can be argued with. A name cannot.
You carry a soul lantern. Light it wherever you rest and you will have company. It will be lit for whoever you decide.
A plain torch. It will not light a Withren lantern, but I will not tell it so. It is doing its best.
You hold a soul torch. Good. It is the only honest flame in the valley. Keep it low and nothing will trouble you.
You hold nether wart as if it might wake. It will not. It likes to be held. Most things grown here do.
Ash-ink fades a little faster in a happy year. I do not know why. I have decided not to worry, and to repaint more often.
A sign should be repainted before it fades, not after. After, you are guessing at a person. Before, you are only tidying.
When a child chooses a name from me, the stole is lighter by one mark and I walk a little taller. Nobody has noticed. Good. It is not their weight to notice.
I keep a ledger of unkept names. I read each aloud once, so none goes a whole Vigil unspoken. It takes a very long time. I do not rush it.
People bring me their keepings to check the spelling. Half are wrong. I correct them gently. Nobody has ever thanked me. I did not take up the stole for thanks.
I know every face in {village} and every name on the Wall. The trouble is joining them. Some faces look exactly like a sign I painted last Vigil.
There is a corner of the Wall nobody walks. I paint it anyway. Somebody ought to know it is there.
When the Wall runs out I draw the new length by hand, a line at a time, before a stone is set. It must feel like it was always going to be there.
I lettered {kept}'s sign myself when I was young. I misjudged the room, and the last letter is squeezed. I love that sign the more for it.
My hood is not for secrecy. It is for the ash that falls while I letter. A good Remembrancer wears the ash and the hood both.
A name has three parts: who they were, whom they loved and who keeps them. I can letter two without asking. The third is the work.
I have a sign reserved on the Wall for myself. I intend to arrive at it late.
Sometimes the letters go on easily, and sometimes slowly, as if the person were thinking it over. I have decided that is courtesy.
Do you know how long it takes to learn every name on a Wall? A lifetime. And then the Wall grows.

replies.text: All of them, as of the last Vigil. The newest I am still learning. They are shy, as new names are.
Yes. Start with the first sign, in the low corner. Oselle. Say it with me. Again. There. Now one more person in the world knows it.

chatter.text: I would like to paint a sign for every Hollowed I have ever met. I never learned their names, so I would leave the sign blank with one mark on it. The mark means: someone was here.

replies.text: You may hold the pot. Hold it steadily. That is as much of the work as the brush.
A single upright stroke with a smaller one across it. It is all a mark can promise.
*sets the brush down* Then you will not be on mine. That is all I have to say.

chatter.text: Do not let the ash settle on you if you can help it. It gets into your name, and then into your signature, and then somebody has to correct the Wall.
A good watch is mostly standing very still and thinking of something else. I think of {kept}. It is excellent for the posture.
The ribs on my chest chafe. We say that is the point. I say the point could be somewhere less tender.
The empty sockets in my circlet catch the lantern-light. People ask whether I am missing something. I am. Three things. Their names are on the plinths.
I have stood at the lane's end so long that the soul sand has begun to hold my prints. Even the sand does the work, now.
An outsider tried to enter the Hall with a pickaxe once. I asked what they wanted to dig. They said a hole. I led them to the terraces and gave them a hoe. They are still digging, and very happy.
I salute the Cairnback at the gate, since it was here before I was. It does not return the salute. It is still senior.
At the end of a watch I say the names of the Three, the name I keep, and the name of whoever takes over. It is the only handover we have, and the only one we need.
Some outsiders mistake us for the Hollowed from behind. We have learned to carry a lantern and to wave it. It helps a great deal.
I am told I look severe. I am only listening hard.
The basalt is heavy at the start of a watch and lighter at the end. Either I grow stronger or the watch grows shorter. I assume the first.
I know the step of every Ashwarden in this Vigil. If a strange step comes down the lane, I know it at once. Yours I learned in a few visits. It is a good step.
We drill for a fight we hope never to meet. It is the most expensive kind of practice, and the only kind worth having.
They told me the first lesson of the watch is patience, the second is that nobody comes, and the third is that somebody always comes. I am still on the second.

replies.text: It is quiet. People call the quiet dull, and then they leave, which is how I know the quiet is working.

replies.ask: I hope you stay on it.
replies.text: Thank you. So do I. A second lesson that lasts is the best a watch can ask.

chatter.text: There is a bench at the valley's edge that nobody uses. It is for any of us who walks out of the old fortresses whole. Every watch, I look. It is always empty.

replies.text: So do I. I have never said it aloud. Thank you for saying it first.
Walk with me, then. Slowly. The lane is a better road with two.
*a long stillness* You may be right. Do not say it again within the walls.

chatter.text: I never fear the Hollowed for what they are. I fear that one of them might look back at me and know me. Better to guard the lane.
Lean, do not sit, on the watch. There is a difference, and no Ashwarden will tell you what it is.
A lantern does not go out because the fire is weak. It goes out because the fire is lonely. I sit by the dim ones for a while. It often helps.
I carry a long hook for the high lanterns and a short one for the low. The short one is for kneeling. Some of the lanterns I kneel to.
Iron is dear here. Every lantern frame is counted, and I count them last of all, in case one has wandered off.
The lane holds only so many lanterns. The rest of the Wall is lit by hand, in turn, one Vigil each. Nobody stays dark for long.
I lit a lantern the wrong way round once, with its sign to the wall. Nobody noticed but the lantern. I turned it and apologised aloud.
In the Hall I light three lanterns first, and then a fourth for whoever is forgotten. Three alone belong to the Three, and are best left to them.
A soul fire does not flicker in a draught. It sways, slowly, like something thinking. The old keepers say that when it leans toward you, someone is saying your name.
A lantern lit in grief burns pale. One lit in love burns bright. One lit from habit burns steady, and that is the one I trust.
I clean the lanterns by hand, never with a cloth. A cloth is too quick. A name should be touched slowly.
If you ever light a lantern here, say whom it is for before you set it down. A lantern lit for nobody goes out of embarrassment.
A lantern is a promise with a handle.
I count the lanterns to calm myself. It does not work. I lose my place at the ones I love.
I know the order in which the lanterns go out. When they go out of order, I go and see why. It is usually a draught. It is sometimes a name.
I once found a lantern at the valley's edge, half buried and still burning. Nobody could say whose it was. I kept it lit, and the Remembrancer lettered a sign for it. The sign says: Someone.

replies.text: It is only a sign. But I go and trim it first, now. I do not tell the others.

replies.ask: Should you not put it out?
replies.text: Whose fire was I to put out? I have not that many fires to spare. No.

chatter.text: I light {kept}'s lantern first and speak to it last. It is the wrong order, and I have never put it right.
Do not set your own lantern near the Name Wall unless you have a name ready. The Wall will ask, quietly. It is rude to have nothing to say.
I check the crowns and only encourage the nubs. The knots in between I leave alone. They are at the age where nobody wants to be watched.
I keep the seed in a bone box against my ribs until planting. It likes the warmth, or it likes the company. The distinction has never mattered to the wart.
I save seed from the best crown of every row. Over the years the wart has come to resemble us. It is stubborn, slow, and very good at standing in the same place.
The Cairnback eats the ripe ones first and the ripe ones only. Its judgement is better than mine. I have started to follow it down the rows.
Cold Terrace grows the palest wart and the sweetest. Low Terrace grows the darkest and strongest. The Crooked Row grows whatever it likes.
I talk to the wart in the voice I use for names. It does not seem to mind, and the yield is good. I am not saying the two are related.
A bad crop is not a failure. It is a message. Usually the message is: you stepped on me.
A good grower can tell the age of a row by its smell. Old rows smell of waiting. Young rows smell of impatience. Both are welcome.
My knees have become the terraces. By which I mean they ache in exactly the shape of the slope.
The wart does not like to be watched. Stare at a row and it stops. Look at the roof of rock and it grows. I have tested this by not looking.
Never step between the rows. If you must cross, cross at the stone, and say sorry to the wart as you go.

replies.text: Good. The wart will say nothing, which is the highest praise it has.
It is only a plant. Step on it and see whose feet hurt. Mine will, first.

chatter.text: A child once asked me whether wart grows from the dead. I said it grows from the sand, which is made of the dead. The child said, so yes. I could not argue. I still cannot.

replies.text: I think so as well. I have never said it to the Remembrancer. It may be our little secret, and a harmless one.
It is a field. Everything that grows anywhere grows from something that lived. We are only honest about it.

chatter.text: I plant a row for {kept} every Vigil. Not to eat. Only a line of wart with their sign at the end of it, growing slowly. It is the nearest thing to a gift they will ever get from me.

replies.text: Yes. One seed, to the first joint. Say a name over it. If it grows, I will tell you whose it was.
I do not know. I plant it all the same. Not knowing is a poor reason to stop.

chatter.text: I worry about blight. There is no blight here. I worry anyway. It is how you tell a grower from someone who merely owns terraces.
On my rounds of the terraces I step on the same stone every time. It is worn smooth. I am told that is a record.
I do not mind the Cairnback in the wart. I mind that it eats the wart and looks pleased. That is the difference between a pest and a colleague.
I make flutes from the long bones of valley beasts. Each plays one low note. A set of flutes is a chord, and a chord is a kind of conversation.
A bone knows how it wants to be cut. Cut against it and it goes pale and hates you. I listen with my thumb.
I never carve a face. Faces we remember. A carved face would be the first thing we forgot to look at.
The dust gets into everything. I have eaten some, I am told. I am no worse for it, and a good deal better informed about the valley.
Every toggle I make differs a little from the last, so that no two Withren wear the same. Nobody has noticed. That is how I like it. The difference is where the thumb finds it.
A child brought me a bone and asked for a sword. I carved a spoon. They were cross at first. They have used it ever since.

replies.text: It is. Most useful things are a disappointment at first. I try to remember that when I am cross.
A sword has one use and it is not a kind one. The spoon has fed a child. We are not comparing like with like.

chatter.text: Valley bone is brittle at first and then it settles. A bone remembers being a beast long after the beast has forgotten. I like to give it a second use.
The plinths in the Hall were the hardest thing I ever made. Each took a year. Each is a little crooked on purpose. A perfect plinth would feel like a boast.
The Weft would pay anything for good bone. I tell them it is not for sale. They ask again, with four hands. I am running out of ways to say no politely.
Nothing is thrown away. Shavings go to the wart, dust to the brewery, offcuts to the children. The children make a ghastly use of them.
I carved a tiny Cairnback once from an offcut. It sits on my bench and does not move, which makes it the most accurate Cairnback ever made.
I tap each bone before I cut. If it rings, I carve it. If it thuds, I thank it and put it back.
I am not allowed to carve in the Hall. I am allowed to sand. I sand with great feeling.
Stand back from the bench, please. The dust is old, and I would not like it to get ideas about you.
Do not pick up a bone to look at it unless you know where it came from. I ask everyone. Everyone puts it down. It is very good manners.
Learning to carve takes a long time. Learning when to stop takes longer. I am told I am still learning the second.
I carved a flute for {kept}, in case they ever want to play. It lies on my hearth. It has never sounded a note, and I have never been disappointed.

replies.text: I have wondered. Sometimes the air in the room is very still, as if someone were deciding. I do not look. It would stop them.
Yes. I would need to know what note you are. Come back when you know. Most people take a long time.

chatter.text: Every brew has a first taste. I take it myself. If I fall over, it is not ready. I have been falling over less lately.
Wart wants a slow fire. Blaze powder wants a fast one. The whole art of brewing is not mixing the two up.
Glass is rare in the valley. Every bottle is kept like a name. I rinse each one and I thank it.
I make a thin, bitter draught for the tired. It does not help anyone rest. It lets them finish the thought they were in the middle of.
People ask me for a brew to forget. We do not have one. We have a brew to remember better, and it tastes worse, which I take as proof.

replies.ask: May I try the remembering one?
replies.text: If you must. It tastes of ash and regret and a little of the pot. Sip slowly. You may find some things you left behind.
It is kinder. It is also a smaller way to be alive. I would not take it from you. I would not offer it, either.
*stirs once, coldly* No. Not here. Go and ask the Ghastkin.

chatter.text: I let nobody stir for me. I let anybody stir for themselves. It is the same pot and a very different brew.
The pots crack from the heat. I keep every shard. I have a shelf of broken pots, each with a name. They are the only crockery I trust.
A brew can go wrong in three ways. It can burn, it can go flat, or it can go quiet. Quiet is the one to fear.
A pot of Mending takes as long to make as the wound takes to heal. If you are in a hurry, do not be hurt.

replies.text: Good. Mending is for the careless, and I would like you to be neither.

replies.ask: How long for a deep wound?
replies.text: Longer than any pot can hold. For those we sit with the hurt one, and the brew helps with the waiting.
A brew cannot be hurried and a wound cannot be hurried. You can only be rude to both.

chatter.text: The brewery is warm because the pots are hot, not because we love people. That is what I tell them. They stay until the pots go cold.
I do not serve grief. I serve a hot cup and a free bench. What people bring to the bench is their own affair.

replies.text: That is the most popular order. Sit. Nobody will ask why.
Hot, bitter and free. Mind the rim. It remembers every mouth.

chatter.text: I pour the Hall's first brew the same way every Vigil, and every Vigil it comes out a little different. I have stopped trying to mend it.
Please do not taste from the pots. Last Vigil someone sipped the wrong one and spoke only in names for a long while. It was lovely, but the Remembrancer would not stop weeping.
I once brewed something for {kept}, from what the Wall says they liked. It was a disaster. I poured it onto the soul sand. The wart grew taller there. I take that as approval.
I keep a ladle for each brew and I have lost track of which is which. I taste and I guess. So far I have been right more often than not.
Our cooks know eleven ways to cook wart. The twelfth is to leave it raw, and it is by far the most popular.
At every meal I set a second bowl for {kept}. They never eat. I never waste it.

replies.text: It is only a habit. A habit is a kindness that has stopped asking whether it is worth it.

replies.ask: What do you do with it?
replies.text: I eat it afterwards. They would insist. They have never said so, but I know them.

replies.ask: That is a waste of food.
replies.text: Waste is a kind of forgetting. I will not be lectured on it by someone who has never kept anyone.

chatter.text: Ash-bread is baked on a hot slab and scorched on purpose. The scorch is the taste. The scorch is also, I am told, the point.
Ash broth is for the sick and the sad. The sick improve. The sad ask for more.

replies.text: In the brewery, in the corner nearest the pot. Sit, and be sick or sad, whichever you are.
It is not good. It is necessary. Those are different, and the second is more reliable.

chatter.text: Nobody here eats much. Eating is a short business: a bowl, a name, done. The talk afterwards is long.
The living should eat. The dead cannot. It is the only unfairness we permit ourselves to complain about.
We do not eat in the Hall. We do not eat on the lane. We do not eat near a Cairnback, which takes it personally. We eat at home, with the door open.
Pickled wart keeps for years. I own a jar older than this lane. I never open it. I only like to know it is there.
The Piglins eat hoglin. We tried it once, for politeness. It was greasy, loud and impossible to argue with.
I have heard that outsiders hold a thing called a feast: many dishes, one meal. I should like to see one. I should like to sit very far from it.
The Wall says {kept} could not abide pickled wart. I eat it every Vigil out of spite, and out of love, in about equal parts.
The valley is the coolest corner of the Nether, and still warm enough to bake bread on a bench. Do not sit on the benches for long.
We do not sweat. There is very little of us left to sweat with. It is the one advantage of being mostly bone.
Ash holds heat like a grudge. It lets go only when it has made its point.
Beyond the valley the lava glows on the rock roof. The Magmari call that warm. I call it loud.
Soul fire gives light and almost no heat. It is the only honest fire we have. It never pretends to be a hearth.
The brewery is the warmest room in the Vigil and the Hall the coolest. We spend our lives going between them with a lantern, being quiet.
Outsiders complain of the heat. I agree with them. I have complained about it for years, silently, to the basalt. It has not taken my side.
On the warmest stretch of the lane we turn the lanterns low. They do not need the extra fire, and the dead are not cold.
Never leave exactly three of anything in a row: three bowls, three lanterns, three stones. Three belong to the Three. We add a fourth, politely.

replies.text: Because four is a promise that the Three are not alone. It is a very small promise. It costs a bowl.
It is a bowl. The silliness is cheap. The omission would be dear. Do not test it.

chatter.text: Do not whistle in the Hall. The soul sand keeps the sound and plays it back when you least want it.

replies.text: Whatever you whistled. Slightly flat. In someone else's voice. Do try not to find out.
Then not here, please. It is very difficult to explain to the Hall.

chatter.text: Never say a name as you step from a stone onto soul sand. The sand catches it and holds on. You will not have that name back for a whole Vigil.
If a lantern gutters when you say a name, the name has been heard. If it does not, say it again, louder, and hope for the best.
A Cairnback that turns its face toward you is counting you. If it counts you twice, you owe someone a visit.
Never pour out the last of a brew. It belongs to the one who is not there.
Never carve bone while a Hollowed is in sight of the valley. The bone remembers whose it was, and carves itself badly.
If you drop a lantern, do not pick it up with your left hand. The left hand is for names and the right for lanterns. I cannot explain it. I will not break it.
Do not run on the Ash Stair. It was cut for people on their way to grieve, and they do not run. The stair takes offence, and then the stair takes your ankle.
We never speak the name of something that is hunting us. We call it the visitor. So far the visitor has been very polite.
Never wear soul-cloth inside out. The seams hold the names you have said. Turned out, they spill.
Set a bowl on the Name Wall and a name goes missing from it. I have not tested this. I do not intend to.
Our oldest Cairnback is called Eventually. It lives up to the name. We name them for what we wish of them: Patience, Not Yet, Later. They are no worse for the wishing.

replies.text: Not yet. Come back when one has chosen you. They choose by standing beside you for a very long time.
It is the best of them. It arrives wherever it is going. That is more than most of us manage.

chatter.text: A young Cairnback has no fire at first. The first spark comes when it first feels safe. Some take a Vigil. Some take longer. We hurry none of them.
When a young Cairnback's fire first catches, we gather, say nothing, and eat. It is the nearest thing we have to a feast.

replies.ask: I would like to see that.
replies.text: Then come back when one is near. We do not announce it. A Cairnback decides in its own time, and so does a guest.
It is very quiet. People mistake it for dull. Then they stay, and it is not.

chatter.text: The bowl on a Cairnback's back is warm, never hot. The children warm their hands on it. The Cairnback permits it, as it permits most things, by not noticing.
A Cairnback does not walk to a place. It arrives at it. This may take a Vigil. When it finally comes, we all look up, surprised, as if it had never been expected.
I tried to count the plates on a Cairnback's shell once. I got a different number each time. I think it rearranges them when nobody is looking. I admire that.
A Cairnback hates being rushed and loves being stood beside. I have stood beside the same one so long that it steps aside for me. Or I for it. We cannot tell.
Behind the Cairnback in a procession, the dead follow. In front of it, nobody dares go.
The fire on its back burns neither bowl nor bone. It burns something the Cairnback gives. I do not ask what. It would be rude to a fire.
I watched a Piglin try to push a Cairnback once. The Piglin gave up. The Cairnback did not notice that anything had been attempted.
If a Cairnback's fire flares for no reason, somebody has said its name kindly. They like that. So do I.
A Cairnback will not be ridden, and will not be pushed. It can be asked. The asking takes a whole watch, and you must mean it.
A Piglin came to the valley's edge, looked at the Wall from a distance, and left a gold nugget on a rock. We did not touch it. It is still there. Nobody knows what it means.

replies.text: Perhaps. It would be a strange one. Gold is not what we offer back. But we noticed it, and that is a kind of reply.
*a very long look* Then take it, and carry it out of the valley, and do not come back with it in your pack.

chatter.text: I heard a Piglin horn from the far ridge. It is a noisy, hopeful sound. I wish I could dislike it more.
A Piglin once offered me gold for a name. I said the name was not for sale. They said everything has a price. I asked the price of their own name. They left.
The Piglins count their dead in gold. We count ours in names. Neither is better. Names are lighter to carry.
On the far shore, where the rock meets the lava sea, I once saw a Magmari standing and glowing. We nodded. It was the best conversation I have ever had with one.
The Magmari ask a toll to cross anything. I would pay it once, only to see their faces when I offered a name in place of payment.
I saw a Weft on the warped ridge once, working all four hands at the same time, and for a moment I forgot to be angry. I remembered again, quickly.
The Weft say the forest is the warp and they are the weft. We have a saying too: the Wall is the warp, and the names are the weft. I did not know I was copying until I said it aloud.
I once watched a Weft pour a drink, stir it, write a letter and wave goodbye in one motion. I am still recovering.
A ghast drifted over the Vigil. Everyone stopped speaking until it had passed. It was not hostile. It was crying. We bowed. It did not notice. It was still the right thing to do.

replies.ask: Do you bow to every ghast?
replies.text: Every one. They were somebody. A bow costs nothing, and the ghast cannot argue.
*very quietly* Then you have not understood what it is. Please do not say that here.

chatter.text: A Ghastkin once left a tear-vial on our boundary stone. We left it there. It is still full. Nobody has the courage to throw it out or to open it.

replies.text: That is what we decided. It is a gift we do not know how to accept, and that is the only kind worth having.
A grief that was theirs, and is now ours to keep out of. Not a bad arrangement.

chatter.text: A Ghastkin never says goodbye. They say, until the next grief. It is the most honest farewell I have heard. I do not like it.
I envy the Ghastkin one thing: they never forget how to be kind, even when they forget everything else. I would give a great deal to be as forgetful about being cross.
Ghastkin children cannot cry yet. Ours cannot keep yet. It is the one thing we share: a time when both of us are too small for the family business.
The Piglins spend their dead, the Magmari ferry them, the Weft weave them, the Ghastkin cry them away. We keep ours. We are the worst at letting go and the best at being found.
I used to think the Nether held one kind of grief. Then I met five.
My head is bigger than the rest of me. Grown-ups say I will grow into it. I say they will shrink into theirs.
I am learning my letters. The first ones I learned were for names. The Remembrancer says that is the right order. I think it is only the boring order.
I can count the lanterns on the lane up to a hundred and eleven. After that I lose my place and begin again at someone different.
I tried wart. It was not nice. I tried it again to be sure. It is still not nice. Grown-ups say you learn to like it. I think you learn to stop saying.
The Brewer let me stir a pot. I stirred it very solemnly. It came out purple. The Brewer said purple was not the plan.

replies.text: That is what I said! The Brewer said purple means danger. I said, good danger? They went and sat down.
I am not a child who spills. I am a child who stirs. It is completely different.

chatter.text: I am practising my solemn face in the polished basalt. It does not look solemn. It looks like someone about to sneeze.
Do you know what is under the soul sand? More soul sand. {neighbour} told me. They also told me a lot of other things. I think they were guessing.
When I grow up I want to be an Ashwarden and stand very still. I am already good at the still part. I am working on the grown part.
Or maybe a Lantern-keeper, because you get to climb. Or a Brewer, because you get to taste. Or a Remembrancer, and then I get to tell everyone they are wrong. I have not decided.

replies.text: Yes! Then I can tell {neighbour} they spelled something wrong. I have waited for years.
Then I taste everything. They say you have to wait for the pot, but I do not mind. I am very good at waiting. I am small.

chatter.text: I found a bone in the sand. I asked the Bonecarver if it was a person bone. They said valley beast. I said, are you sure? They said yes. I said sorry to it anyway.
Hollowed and Keepers is not allowed on the lane any more. I fell into a lantern. The lantern is fine. I am fine. The rules are new.
I have a favourite name on the Wall. It is very short. It is Ou. I do not know who Ou was, but they look friendly. Their sign has a little curl.

replies.text: Yes! Say it with me. Ou. Ou. Now there are two of us. Three, counting the Wall.
It is a short name! Short names are the bravest. They have nowhere to hide.

chatter.text: Please do not tell the Cairnback that I sat on it. It is very quiet about being sat on. I think it is waiting to tell everyone itself.

replies.text: Thank you! You are the best secret-keeper. Better than {neighbour}. They tell.
They do? Oh. Did the Cairnback tell? It is very sneaky for something so slow.

chatter.text: The Bonecarver made me a little flute. It plays one low note. It is the note my chest makes when I am sad. I play it when I am not, so it does not feel lonely.
I drew a face in the ash with my finger. The Remembrancer said it looked like someone who had died. I said it was meant to be me. They went very quiet.
Sometimes I whisper my own name to the soul sand, to check that it stays. So far it has. I do not know what I would do if it did not.
I am the youngest in {village}. Everyone else is old and tired. I am old and not tired. It is a very special position.

The grown-ups say when you are older about everything. I asked when I will be older. They said soon. I asked how soon. They said a Vigil. I do not know how long that is. I think it is a very long one.
I was told to be quiet in the Hall. I was quiet. Then I sneezed. It echoed for a long time. Now I think the Three know my sneeze.
Do you have a Name Wall where you come from? Or do you just remember everyone in your head? That sounds very crowded.

replies.text: That sounds hard. You must be very good. Will you teach me how not to forget a name?
Oh. Then who do you say hello to? Is it only the living? That sounds so lonely.
Then build one! Start with one name. Then add another. That is how ours began. Probably.

chatter.text: We have a rule that nobody laughs in front of the Wall. So I laughed behind it. The Wall did not tell. I checked.
