That was a good talk. I do not say that often, and I never say it falsely.
Safe steps. The lane is long, but it is lit.
Away with you, then. I will pretend it was my idea.
Take what you learned. Leave what you broke. We will manage the rest.
Be careful of strangers on the road. They are mostly harmless. Mostly is the whole difficulty.
I will be here. I am nearly always here. It is one of my better qualities.
Go and be alive somewhere. We will remember it for you.
Walk until the lanterns thin. Then a little further. Then come back.
Until later. Later is the word we use for a time we mean to have.

farewell.text: You may go. The lane is that way. It was good of you to stop. I mean that as a fact, not a courtesy.
Farewell. I have your face. I do not yet have your name. I am leaving the gap, in case.
Go on. I will say nothing of this to the Wall. It may say something to me.
Leave by the lantern lane. The other way is shorter, and shorter is not always safer.
Goodbye, stranger. It is a pleasant word. I hope it lasts a while.
Walk well. If we meet again, I will know you. That is all I promise, and I keep my promises.
Come back soon. Sooner than the Hollowed. They never leave, so it is a low bar.
Go on, then. I will say your name once more, quietly, so the lantern knows you are coming back.
Walk gently. I mean it kindly, though it sounds like a warning. In this valley it is both.
Do not be a stranger. Be a visitor. They are easier to keep track of.
Another good talk. I will think it over when the wick runs low.
Return when you like. The bench will keep warm. It is the only one in the Vigil that will.
Go well, and eat something. I say it to everyone I like, and I do not say it to everyone.
I will keep the stool by the lane as it is. Come and break it in properly next time.
Take care. Take more care than seems necessary. The valley has a talent for taking whatever is not guarded.
I will tell {kept} you came. I will tell them you laughed. They will want to hear it twice.
Walk lightly, friend. Look back once at the corner. I will be there. I am always at the corner.
Go, and come back with a story. I have told all of mine, some twice.
Go with my whole name behind you. I have no better thing to give, but it is not a small thing.
I will keep your place in the sayings. I will not move it. You will not find it moved.
Whatever happens out there, come home. The word is yours here. I have told the lanterns.
If you do not return, I will walk out and find you. I do not know the way. I will learn it for you.
Do not hurry back. Do not dawdle either. Be exactly the right amount of late.
Until later, Kept. Your name will be in my mouth before the next lantern needs trimming. It is no trouble at all.
I will set your visit in my ledger under a short entry. The short entries are the ones I reread.
Go, and mind the third stair on your way down. It has ended better arguments than yours.
I will not forget your face. That is a promise I can keep. I have had a great deal of practice.
Farewell. If I lose your name, I will keep the face. If I lose the face, I will keep the way you left.
Go. I put a small mark in the margin of my stole where you stood. It may be fanciful. It is also permanent.
When you are gone I will go back to the Wall and say the next sign. It will be a little warmer for having heard you.
I will mark you off the post as you go. I do not like marking people off. Come back and be marked on again.
The lane is clear. I looked. I always look. It is the only kind of kindness I am licensed for.
You are free to go. I was not holding you. I was only watching you not go.
Move along, then. The post stands between us. I am, as always, very glad of the post.
Safe road. I will give the post a rest while you cross the lane. Do not tell anyone.
Go, and look behind you once. I will be there. I am always the one standing.
Take the middle of the lane. The lanterns will light you to the bend. After that it is you and the dark.
I will leave your lantern burning a moment longer. It is a habit. It can hurt nothing but the oil.
Go on, then. Mind the posts. They have no feelings, but I do.
Away with you. The wick wants me, and I want the wick. It is a simple romance.
I will keep a lantern low for you at the end of the lane. A friend's lantern is the cheapest kind to keep.
Go well. I trimmed one wick short and one long, so the lane will tell me which way you went.
Walk round the terrace, not through it. It is slower. It is also why the wart is still there.
Go gently. The wart enjoyed your visit. You will never hear it say so.
Off you go. I have a row to see to. It will not see to itself, though it has tried.
Mind the shoots by the gate. They look like weeds. They are not. They are very sensitive weeds.
Come back when the shoots are tall. I will show you where they hid. They like to surprise visitors.
I will save you the best of the crop, or the second best. The best is sacred, and not quite mine.
Mind the bone dust on your way out. It clings. Think of it as being briefly and harmlessly famous.
Go, and tell no one the shape of what I am carving. I have not yet told it myself.
Farewell. I have a post to finish. It has been very patient. I am ashamed of how patient.
Come and see me when I have a finished thing. Until then I am only making a mess, with intent.
Take a shaving. It will not mean anything. Keep it anyway. All my best work began as a shaving.
I will make something while you are away and pretend it is for no one. Then I will give it to you.
Take a little warmth with you. Not in a bottle. In a thought. Bottles break.
The pot wants me. It has opinions. Go well.
Stay out of the brewery draught on your way out. It carries more than smell.
Goodbye. If you feel strange later, it was not my brew. It was the valley.
Come and taste the next batch. I will not warn you it is bad. I will only warn you it is mine.
Go, but keep room for the next cup. I will pour it full. Whenever you arrive, it will be warm.
Bye. I did not talk to you. Do not tell my parent. Actually I did. I talked a lot. It was nice.
Go on. I will wave at the Cairnback instead of you. It does not wave back, so I never feel silly.
Bye bye. Stay out of the Hall. I mean it. I only went in once and I was not caught.
You are leaving? Fine. I was going to leave first. I just had not started yet.
Come back soon! I will keep thinking of questions. I have eleven so far. They are mostly about skulls.
Do you have to go? I suppose so. I will go and tell the Wall. It will be very bored. Everyone on it is already finished.
Goodbye! I will draw you a picture for when you come back. It is a Cairnback with your face. Is that all right?
Bye! Walk slowly. I always say that, so you will know it is me.
Bye! If you see a Hollowed, wave. Not at it. Beside it. In its general direction.
Goodbye. Have a good adventure. I will stay here and have a good boring.
Go safely! I will be here, practising being solemn. I am getting very good.
Bye! Do not let the soul sand have your boots. It is greedy, for sand.
Come back and tell me everything. Especially the parts you are not supposed to tell.
I am going to count to a very large number, and when I reach it you will be back. It is an extremely large number.
Mind the lanes. If you meet {neighbour}, say I said hello. They will pretend to be busy, which is how they say it back.
Safe road out of {village}. The lanterns give way to dark soon, but it is polite dark.
Leave by the south lane. The posts there are the oldest. They have seen more departures than anyone.
Go. {village} will leave a light on. That is not a manner of speaking. We cannot turn them off.
The wart will hush as you pass. Do not take it personally. It does that for everyone.
The valley is yours. I only borrow a patch of it. If you meet a Hollowed, say any name and walk on. They are slow to notice and not unkind.
Walk the ridge, not the hollow. The hollow is where the sand holds on.
Farewell, wanderer. If you pass a cairn nobody tends, add a stone. That is how the dead are kept out here.
Go well. Out here the Hollowed are the only other travellers, and they do not talk. You were the best conversation I have had.
I will watch the valley a little longer. If you are in trouble, shout a name. Any name. Some of them listen.
Keep that skull apart from the others. Apart. Do you hear me? Apart. That is all I ask of you.
Take the star to the Hall. Do not leave it on a shelf. Please. It is three people.
Take your gold with you, if you must. Do not set it down near a lantern. It makes them nervous.
Go and lay that rose on a sign that has none. There are always one or two.
Choose the name for your name tag well. Something will have to answer to it for a long time.
Please take the powder somewhere else. Anywhere else. There are lovely open valleys.
Keep the compass close. May you never need it. May you find it useful anyway.
Keep that totem in your hand, not your pocket. If death is going to be refused, it should be refused quickly.
Hold the lantern high on the dark stretches. Soul fire likes to be seen.
Keep that bed in your pack until you are home. I say it to every outsider. Every outsider forgets.
Go on, and keep your hands where my neighbours can see them. They are shy about hands.
I will think of your face when the lanes are quiet. It is not a promise. The lanes are quiet often.
Look after yourself, because I will be cross if I have to look after the Wall and your sign both.
Walk on, friend. I keep a little of every goodbye, folded small. Yours is quite thick by now.
Farewell. The soul fire at my hearth burned a little higher while you were here. I am not saying it was you. I am not saying it was not.
I will say a name for you at the Wall. I will not say whose. It will be one I am fond of, which is the best I can offer.
You are always leaving. It is almost your best trait. It means you are always going to come back.
Go and be careful. And then be careless, once, in a small way, where no harm can follow. It is good for the heart.

refuse.text: You struck one of us. The Vigil remembers. We remember everything. That is the trouble with us.
No. Not now. Lower your hands and walk away, and the next part will go easier for you.
We have buried better fighters than you. We kept their names. Shall we start a sign for yours?
*a hollow, silent stare* The Vigil remembers.
You would raise a hand in a place of names. I will keep that. I would rather have kept something else.
Speak? To you? Later, perhaps. Much later. We are very patient, and very hard to forget.
Go away! I am telling the Ashwardens! I am telling the Remembrancer! I am telling the WALL!
I do not know you, and now I know the one thing about you I did not want to. Step away. This is the end of the conversation.
No. I will not talk. I will remember, and later I will not be in a hurry about it.
You have made yourself a very short entry in my memory. A single line. It says: struck me.
A stranger's first act was a blow. I am keeping that, gently, in the place where I put things I wish I could lose.
I will not shout. Shouting is for the Hollowed, and they have been quiet a long time. Walk away.
Let us both pretend I am too well-mannered to answer. It is only partly pretending.
I had begun to say your name kindly. Now I will say it carefully. That is a different way to say it.
You came back, and then you did that. I am not angry. I am being very still. Do not mistake it for calm.
I told {neighbour} you were not like the others. I will have to tell them I was wrong. I dislike that sentence.
Do not speak. You have used up the kind of words I would answer.
That was a poor way to be remembered. It is how you will be, for a while.
Step back. Hands low. Whatever you meant, it did not read as a visit.
I wrote your name in ash. I am looking at it now, and it is smudging. Do not give me reason to wipe it away.
I would have said yes to nearly anything you asked. I wish you had asked.
You struck a friend. That is the trouble with striking friends. They remember it as a friend.
I am not going to hit you. I am going to stand here and let you think about what you did. Take your time. I have a great deal.
I told {kept} about you. I will have to go and tell them the rest. I do not know how I will say it.
You hurt me, and I cannot quite make myself angry. That is the worst part. Go away until I can.
Leave me room to remember who you were before this. It is a short walk. I would like to take it alone.
Kept. I said your name when I rose. I will say it again at the hearth, and I do not know in what voice.
You are the one person I would not have braced for. So I was not braced. That is how it landed.
I will not strike back. I will not speak either. I will sit with {kept} and ask what to do. They will not know. It will still help.
Even now I keep your name. That is the terrible part of the rule. I cannot put it down, and I cannot say it kindly.
Go away, for now. Not forever. I do not have that word for you. I am only asking for a little of the quiet you broke.
If you meant it, I will find that out later and it will break something. If you did not, I will find that out too. Until then, no.
Dear one. I will say it once, and then I will be silent. It is the last thing I give you until this is mended.

refuse: No. Not after that. Go, and let the quiet do what words cannot.
I will not answer. It is the one courtesy I have left, and I am spending it now.
Lower your hand. Lower your voice. Raise your feet, and take them elsewhere.
You have chosen your answer already. I am only letting you hold it a while.
Not now, and not soon, and perhaps not ever. We keep the long memory. It is our inheritance.
We do not forgive quickly. We do not curse either. We keep, and keeping is a very patient thing.

refuse.text: I will letter this as well: the place, the blow, your face. It is a long entry. I am sorry you are the subject.
Every blow is a name nobody wanted to write. I will have to write yours, in a different ink.
I wrote you into my ledger with a good pen. I am going to need a worse one.
I am bound to be exact, not unkind. You raised a hand. I will meet it. The post is behind me. Mind it.
Walk away. That is the whole of my advice. Past that point my training takes over, and it is not subtle.
I swore to guard everyone who walks my lanes. I did not swear to enjoy it. Walk away before I learn which oath is stronger.
Step away from the lanterns. If one goes out because of you, I will know whose name you put out, and I will not forgive it.
I carry a lit lamp and a very steady hand. Do not make me use both for the wrong thing.
Get off my terrace. You have hurt me and, worse, you are standing on my wart.
I have dug soul sand all my life. I am stronger than I look. I am considerably less patient.
I carve bone for a living. I know exactly where it breaks. Walk away.
My chisel is in my hand. I will not use it. I will only hold it where you can see it, and let you decide.
I have a pot at a rolling boil behind me. I do not want to explain how I might use it. Please spare us both.
That tasted nothing like a visit. Go, before I add you to a recipe.
*backs behind a Cairnback* It will not move for you. It never moves for anyone. That is the whole point of it.
My parent said outsiders hit. I said no. Now I have to say I was wrong, and they will be so smug.
I do not want to talk to you. I want to be somewhere else. Somewhere with fewer fists.
You are loud and you hit things, and the Wall is going to know. It always knows. It is just very slow about telling.
I thought you were nice! Now I have to unthink it. It takes ages.
I am not scared. My knees are doing something, but I am not scared.
Go away. I am counting to a hundred. If you are still here I will tell the Remembrancer, and they never forget.
I thought we were friends. That is what I get for thinking. I am going to go and sit very still and be disappointed.
You are in the middle of {village}. All of {village} heard that, and all of it has a long memory. Choose your next step carefully.
The lanterns went still when you struck. They are watching. I would not give them a second thing to remember.
There are Ashwardens near. I have not called them. I am giving you the length of this sentence to leave. It was a short sentence.
Out here there is no Wall and no one to hear. That makes it worse, not better. A thing done unseen is still kept.
There are only two of us in this valley. I would prefer it were one. Go.
You chose a quiet place to strike. I will remember it quietly. The valley will help me.
You strike us with a Hollowed skull in your pack? You are asking for the worst answer we have. Put it down, and then leave.
You carry three souls and raise a hand. Choose which of the two you are. Then put the other down.
Gold, and a blow. You have been learning from the Piglins. It is not a compliment.
